mutations.before: `select 1 from campaign where org_id = $1 and slug = $2 and deleted_at is null for share`
mutations.after: `select 1 from campaign where org_id = $1 and slug = $2 for share`
mutations.because: the slug-branch deleted_at filter is what refuses a tombstoned campaign addressed by slug (the common case: every route reaches a campaign by slug until PT-5). Dropping it lets enqueueJob insert a job for a deleted campaign, so `enqueueJob refuses a tombstoned campaign by slug` (which asserts rejects.toBeInstanceOf(CampaignGoneError)) stops rejecting and the claim is admitted instead — the test goes red. The uuid branch carries its own deleted_at clause a few lines above (matched by `id = $2::uuid`, not `slug = $2`), so this anchor is unique and lands on the slug branch alone.
command: enqueueJob refuses a tombstoned campaign by slug
